# Paccekabuddhaapadāna (Tha-Ap 2)
**ID:** Tha-Ap 2
**Section:** Therāpadāna (tha-ap)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paccekabuddhaapadāna* (also attested as *Paccekabuddhāpadāna*) is the second chapter of the *Therāpadāna* in the Pali *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Appleton 2010; Buswell & Lopez 2014; SuttaCentral]. Forming one of the introductory verse sections of the *Apadāna* directly following the *Buddhāpadāna*, the text features verses attributed to the Buddha describing the distinctive qualities, accomplishments, and merits of solitary buddhas (*paccekabuddha*; Sanskrit *pratyekabuddha*), who attain awakening without an external teacher and do not teach [Appleton 2010; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. SuttaCentral records five translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
The text is intimately linked to early poetic literature on solitary ascetics. A vast majority of its verses (§9.4–50.4) directly correspond to the *Khaggavisāṇa Sutta* (*Snp* 1.3, §1.1–41.4) with high textual overlap, and are thoroughly embedded in the canonical commentary *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (*Cnd* 23) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes connections and shared stanzas across early Buddhist literature, including the Gāndhārī *Rhinoceros Sūtra* (GF 5B), the *Mūlasarvāstivādivinaya*, the *Dhammapada* (dhp 328–329), the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), and various Chinese parallels (such as MA 72 and Dharmapada parallels T 210, T 212, and T 213) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently confirms extensive text reuse in the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as close alignments with Sanskrit parallels in the *Mahāvastu Avadāna* and the *Patna Dharmapada* [DharmaNexus].
